chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Diet, health and what people eat
summary: Caldwell and Dance compare modern food rules with his long-lived father and discuss quitting smoking.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, you know, Stanley (unintelligible) of these things, what you should be, what you should be, so I realize that I really just -- now, when I was a kid, my father and brother -- he was a big, husky fellow about six feet, 200 and some pounds, about 235 -- I said, but never been but -- hearty eater all of us, in fact, was a hearty eater, and his sister, but he lived to be 96, had his natural set of teeth. And I read these things sometimes, don't eat this, don't eat that, don't eat no butter, don't eat no sugar, don't put no cream in your milk. I said, well, what the hell is going on.
Now, I look back on these, reading all these things, and, you know, reminiscing about back there when I was a kid, never heard of all this.
Well, the only thing, you know, the only thing, I think, is that back when you're talking of most people -- a lot of people worked with their bodies physically.
And, you know, they walked more.

And now you use -- you get in a cab, you get your car or you -- but I mean I think if you were working on a farm with a plow or something, well, you could eat any damn thing you liked, and it wouldn't put any weight on.

It's the fact that you're sitting down so much today. And there are a lot -- I had a checkup recently, and the doctor said, well, you're five pounds heavier than last time. I said, yeah, but I haven't smoked since Christmas. So he said, well, I'd rather you put five pounds on than smoke. So, you know, you knock off smoking, and then your appetite bothers you, so then you put on weight and have a heart attack instead of dying of lung cancer. So --
Yeah, that's what they claim too.
